title: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali
author: patanjali
attributionNote: Traditionally ascribed to Patanjali. The text was probably compiled from earlier material over several centuries, and its classical commentary is later than the sutras themselves.
description: The four books of the Yoga Sutras set out the discipline of stilling the mind: the modifications of consciousness, the obstacles to practice, the powers that follow concentration, and the isolation of the seer from what is seen. Charles Johnston's 1912 edition prints each sutra with an interpretive commentary.
historicalContext: The foundational text of the Yoga school, composed in Sanskrit and transmitted with a commentary attributed to Vyasa. Johnston's edition was written for general readers and presents the sutras as a sequence of spiritual aphorisms rather than as a philological edition.
availabilityNote: Streamed from Project Gutenberg at read time: the whole plain-text edition is fetched and split at the chapter headings it prints. The 1912 translation by Charles Johnston is public domain in the United States.
